driverRegime.method: daily % change of each asset regressed on the daily change in the US 2-year and 10-year yields (basis points) and on the daily % change in WTI; a driver is dominant when |corr| >= 0.4

dataNotes: Run timing: this cycle ran the morning of Friday 20 November 2026 after the GitHub Actions fetch job drafted contracts/*.2026-11-19.json from Thursday 19 November's close. Every figure used is dated at or before 2026-11-19; Intuit, Ross Stores, Gap, Elastic and Anthropic after-hours moves are dated 19 November. News-log entries dated 20 November (Asia's sell-off, Friday gold/bitcoin moves) were NOT used.

Bonds, dollar and IWM sigma are not auto-fetched; the last obtainable implied-volatility values (TLT 30-day IV, EUR/USD 1-month ATM IV, RVX) were carried forward again with stale-source notes. The fetched ^VIX (28.44), ^GVZ (28.70) and ^VXN (36.48) sigma gauges are dated 19 November.

News-log entries for 2026-11-19 (four, matching the Artifact database exactly; already present in data/news_log.json; no hand-entered entries) were read. Session wraps from CappNotes ('Closing Look - Thursday, November 19, 2026'), Strategitz ('Global Markets Close - November 19, 2026') and StockTitan ('Stock Market Today, November 19, 2026') supplied indexes, breadth, sectors, VIX, yields, FX, metals/oil, credit, ETF flows, Kalshi/FedWatch pricing, economic data, the Anthropic debut and movers. AAII's 19 November release could not be obtained; the week-ending-11-November reading is used. EUR/USD and the MOVE index were not obtainable.

Vendor conflicts: gold's session change is -3.04% to $3,628.30 late-session (CappNotes) vs -3.22% on the fetched GC=F close (3737.9 -> 3617.7); the fetched close is used. The dollar index is 103.88 (CappNotes) vs 103.95 (Strategitz) vs a fetched 103.92. VIX closed 28.44 (CappNotes, matching the fetched close) vs 28.31 (Strategitz). Anthropic's IPO raise is $81.3B (CappNotes, StockTitan) vs $107.3B (Strategitz) - the lower figure, matching the news log, is cited. CappNotes gives the high-yield spread +4bp on the day but '+24bp over three sessions'. ES=F fell 2.50% and NQ=F 3.34% on fetched closes vs the cash indexes' -2.02% and -2.21%, because the prior futures closes were struck at a different time from Wednesday's cash close; the fetched closes are used.

Category 1-12 votes are neutral unless a dated source gives a clear read: Breadth (1D) is bearish for the three equity assets on the 37/464 S&P 500 split, all 11 sectors down and small caps worst; Credit (1D) is bearish for the equity assets on three sessions of high-yield widening (plus neo-cloud private-credit tightening for the Nasdaq-100); Earnings (1D) is bearish for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 on the AI reversal (Nvidia, AMD, Anthropic's fade) and Intuit/Ross after-hours drops; Rates (1D) and Cross-asset (1D) are bullish for Treasuries on the fourth straight 10-year decline and the risk-off tape; Fed path is hawkish horizon-wide (Kalshi 89.3% / FedWatch 96.4% for a 25bp December hike) - bearish for equities, Treasuries and gold, bullish for the dollar; Cross-asset (1D) is bearish for gold (silver, copper, crypto liquidation; Bespoke's fastest three-month decline since 2013), bullish for the dollar (EM and commodity-FX weakness) and bearish for the Nasdaq-100 (TAIEX -4.40%); Sentiment (5D/10D) is a contrarian bullish vote for the equity assets on AAII's 51.4% bearish reading; Positioning (5D/10D) is bullish for the S&P 500 on JP Morgan's ~20th-percentile aggregate US positioning, neutral for the Nasdaq-100 where light hedge-fund tech exposure offsets ~80th-percentile semis exposure. Oil was flat, so the S&P 500's and Russell 2000's dominant oil driver gives no read. Trend structure follows the computed structure reads; Market structure carries its own mechanical direction.
